clue.text: Bridge expert in court

definitions.meaning: Sir Donald ... was the engineer who designed the portable military bridge named after him
a castle's outer courtyard, enclosed by its wall, is called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the surname of the bridge-designing engineer; the other is the walled courtyard of a castle.

clue.text: Badly garbled direction to raise capital

indicators.note: the letters are put together badly, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: E, east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A muddled set of instructions for raising funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise' is only a link: the surface pretends 'raise capital' is about money. The capital is that of Serbia.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital city of Serbia.

clue.text: Swell position for a batsman

definitions.meaning: in cricket the crease is the line where the batsman stands

explanation.definitionFit: To grow larger is to swell; in cricket a batsman standing at the crease line is in that place.

clue.text: They're down to play bingo

parts.note: the caller's cry to begin a bingo game tells players to look down at their cards

explanation.definitionFit: The bingo call 'eyes down' asks players to look at their cards, the organs of sight lowered.

clue.text: Moved camp

explanation.definitionFit: Being emotionally stirred and being artificially showy both share this one word.

clue.text: Rows among allies end in cordiality

indicators.note: says one word goes inside the other, placed among its letters

parts.note: friends are allies
lines are rows

explanation.surface: Arguments between partners finish with warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like quarrels but means lines; 'end in' is only a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordiality and amiability are synonyms for this warm disposition.

clue.text: Archbishop of York has to dress up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: to robe is to dress, put on vestments

explanation.surface: The Archbishop of York must put on his vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archbishop of York signs himself with the abbreviation of Eboracum, the Latin name for York.
explanation.definitionFit: The signature of the Archbishop of York is an abbreviation of the Latin for York.

clue.text: Man of the cloth has a follower, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word for a follower is said aloud, sounding like a different word

parts.note: one who tails or follows someone

explanation.surface: A clergyman has a disciple, it is rumoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of the cloth' suggests a priest, but here it is a man who works with cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cuts and sews cloth into suits is literally a man of the cloth.

clue.text: This helps fishermen bring the catch to the surface

definitions.text: This helps fishermen bring the catch to the surface

parts.words: This helps fishermen bring the catch to the surface
parts.note: an angling lure that floats on the water, tempting fish to rise to it

explanation.definitionFit: An artificial fly that floats on the water lures trout up to take it at the top.

clue.text: Lapped and beaten

definitions.meaning: drank like a cat, passing the tongue over

explanation.definitionFit: A cat drinking uses its tongue this way, and colloquially a thrashed team was also given this treatment.

clue.text: Its members are outnumbered

parts.note: describes the smaller group in any vote or population, whose people are always fewer than the rest

explanation.definitionFit: The smaller part of a group is by definition exceeded in number by the larger part.

clue.text: Discussion with a specialist about coolant units

indicators.note: the letters are turned about, so rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A conversation with an engineer about refrigeration equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting an expert to seek advice is to confer with them.

clue.text: Grass blown in the wind?

definitions.meaning: a tall marsh plant of the grass family
the vibrating strip in a clarinet or oboe, blown in the woodwind section

explanation.definitionFit: A tall marsh grass shares its name with the vibrating sliver that sounds a woodwind instrument.

clue.text: We hear it is healthy

definitions.meaning: what the ears pick up, a noise
in good condition, as in fit and well

explanation.definitionFit: A noise is what reaches the ears, and the same word means in good shape, as in mind and body.

clue.text: I left to start work

indicators.note: says the word 'to' comes at the start, ahead of the other pieces

explanation.surface: Someone announces they have gone off to begin their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' means TO goes first, then I and L follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour and hard graft are synonyms for this kind of strenuous work.

clue.text: It moves the helicopter, up or down

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads the same whether read upwards or downwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A remark on the part that lifts a helicopter up or brings it down.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning blade assembly on top of a helicopter drives it through the air.

clue.text: It has wings and flies

parts.note: in a theatre the sides ... are wings and the space above for scenery is the flies

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's acting platform has wings at the sides and flies overhead for scenery.

clue.text: Record playing in the small hours-mood indigo?

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a record that is on is being played
very late at night, split here as 'so late'

explanation.surface: Someone spins a melancholy jazz record late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mood Indigo' is a Duke Ellington tune; indigo is blue, and a blue mood is a sad one, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a blue mood means feeling dejected and inconsolable.

clue.text: Upset caused by greed and corruption

indicators.note: a corrupted form of the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Distress brought on by avarice and dishonesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused by' is a link; 'and' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset in the sense of mentally unbalanced, disturbed.

clue.text: Clumsy former spouse in Pinter play

indicators.note: says one piece is placed inside the other
the letters of the playwright's name are played with, rearranged

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife

explanation.surface: An ex-partner acting awkwardly in a Harold Pinter drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' is the anagram signal on the playwright's name, and the former spouse goes inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being clumsy is lacking skill, unskilful.

clue.text: Where Jack is the centre of attention

definitions.text: Where Jack is the centre of attention

parts.words: Where Jack is the centre of attention
parts.note: the jack is the small white target ball in bowls, which every player aims at on the lawn

explanation.definitionFit: The lawn used for bowls is where players aim their woods at the small target ball, the jack.

clue.text: It never rains but it pours

definitions.text: It never rains but it pours

parts.words: It never rains but it pours
parts.note: a proverb read literally: a vessel that pours a hot drink but never rains

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel for brewing tea pours from its spout but never produces rain.

clue.text: Transport for student with a university final

indicators.note: says the university letter comes last

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for a student
and means with, together

explanation.surface: A carriage for an undergraduate going up for finals.
explanation.walkthrough: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-drawn carriage was a means of transport.

clue.text: Former graduate returns for a test

parts.note: ex- means former, as in an ex-partner

indicators.note: the word for a graduate is read backwards

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, a graduate degree

explanation.surface: An old alumnus comes back to sit an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A test of knowledge in school or college is commonly called by this short form.

clue.text: Lift shafts, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word for shafts is said aloud to give a word that sounds identical

parts.note: rays, as in shafts of light

explanation.surface: A remark about the vertical tunnels in which elevators run.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to elevate it, put it higher.

clue.text: Such a cat deserves a detailed description

definitions.text: Such a cat deserves a detailed description

parts.words: Such a cat deserves a detailed description
parts.note: 'detailed' read as 'de-tailed', without a tail, which is the defining trait of the breed from the Isle of Man

explanation.definitionFit: The tailless breed of cat comes from the Isle of Man and takes its adjective.

clue.text: In certain charts it may indicate a mile

indicators.note: says the answer sits inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: On some maps a small mark stands for a mile on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a cryptic definition about map scales, but the answer lurks across 'certain charts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Ordnance Survey maps used a scale where one small unit of length on paper stood for a mile.

clue.text: Side of fresh meat

indicators.note: the letters are made afresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: A cut of meat that has not gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: A side in sport is a group of players, a squad.

clue.text: Movingly depict an academic

indicators.note: the letters of the words are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to portray a scholar with feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic in its sense of overly concerned with fine points of learning and rules.

clue.text: The length an association will go to?

definitions.text: The length an association will go to?

parts.words: The length an association will go to?
parts.note: plays on 'go to great lengths': one word is both an old measure of distance, about three miles, and a sporting association

explanation.definitionFit: An old unit of distance of about three miles and a sports association share this word.

clue.text: Moving about?

definitions.meaning: concerning, with regard to, an old-fashioned preposition

explanation.definitionFit: An affecting scene is described this way, and the same word is a dated preposition meaning concerning.

clue.text: Wrongly admits to be at the centre of things

indicators.note: the letters are put together in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses falsely just to get attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the middle of everything is to be among it, surrounded by it.
